title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is navigating a mix of funding boosts and operational hurdles this week. While satellite resilience is getting a budgetary lift, launch risks and technological delays continue to cast a shadow over ambitious plans.

themes.title: Funding for Space Resilience
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup has added $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, signaling a strong commitment to bolstering satellite capabilities. This comes at a time when the Space Force is grappling with rising costs and launch risks, highlighting the need for robust funding.

themes.title: Launch Delays and Risks
themes.body: The hypersonic glide-vehicle test has slipped for the third consecutive quarter, raising questions about the reliability of cutting-edge defense technologies. Meanwhile, the GAO's flagging of satellite costs in the Space Force portfolio underscores the ongoing challenges in managing launch risks.

themes.title: Emerging Players in Space
themes.body: Chinese satellite manufacturer Hongqing's recent $191 million raise reflects the growing competition in the satellite manufacturing sector. Additionally, startups like Verde Technologies are pivoting towards space, indicating a shift in focus among new entrants.

themes.title: Strategic Partnerships and Contracts
themes.body: Anduril and L3Harris are teaming up for a tactical SDA constellation bid, showcasing a trend of collaboration in the defense tech space. Meanwhile, Palantir's $480 million extension on the TITAN ground station program highlights the increasing importance of data management in military operations.
